title: DiDi Pay in China (2026): Foreign Cards, Alipay & WeChat
heading: How to Pay for DiDi in China as a Foreigner (2026)
description: How can foreigners pay for DiDi in China? Compare in-app cards, Alipay and WeChat Pay, prepare a backup and resolve failed or duplicate ride charges.
quickAnswer: Before your first DiDi ride in mainland China, open the actual ride-booking screen and check the payment methods offered to your account. A foreign bank card may work through a supported in-app method or through an Alipay or WeChat Pay wallet that accepts that card, but acceptance varies by account, card issuer, ride product and verification status. Set up the method on Wi-Fi before booking, keep another way to pay, and check the app's trip receipt before paying a driver separately. A card linked to a wallet is not a guarantee that every in-app transaction succeeds.

contentSections.title: Choose a payment route before booking

rows: Card appears as available for your ride and any verification completes
The wallet actually appears in the ride's payment options; linked foreign card works for that purchase
Review that app's own checkout and support flow
Standalone DiDi or official taxi queue

items: Payment methods can differ between the standalone DiDi app, a DiDi mini-program and another app's ride-hailing entry. Check the specific product you will use.
Do not assume that a card saved in Alipay or WeChat Pay automatically becomes a direct card in DiDi.

contentSections.title: Set up and test before the airport ride
items: Download the official app from your device's app store and sign in with a number that can receive verification codes.
On reliable Wi-Fi, add your preferred payment method if the app offers it. Finish any card issuer authentication or wallet verification.
Search for your hotel using its Chinese name or full address, and check the exact terminal pickup zone before requesting a ride.
At checkout, read the selected payment method, displayed estimate and applicable extras. Keep data access available until the trip is completed.
After arrival, use the in-app trip record or receipt to confirm the final charge. Keep a screenshot of the booking ID if you need support later.

contentSections.title: If your payment is declined
items: First confirm whether the charge is pending or completed in both the ride app and your bank; an authorization hold can differ from a final charge.
If authentication fails, check mobile data, SMS access, card limits, expiry date and overseas transaction settings with your issuer.
Try another supported payment method within the same ride flow. Do not repeatedly tap pay if a transaction is still processing.

If the app shows an unpaid trip, use its support or payment screen and keep the trip ID. If a driver asks for an extra off-app payment, clarify whether the ride has already been charged before handing over money.
At an airport, use the staffed official taxi queue if your account cannot complete a ride; prepare your destination in Chinese and confirm how that taxi accepts payment.

contentSections.title: Know what the displayed price covers
items: A pre-ride estimate is not necessarily the final fare. Traffic, route, waiting time, tolls or the product terms may affect the charge shown in the completed trip.
Compare the ride ID, time, route and fee items in the receipt before raising a dispute.
Foreign-card currency conversion and issuer fees may appear separately on your bank statement.
Keep enough time and a second transport choice for a flight or train connection; resolving a declined card at the pickup area can take longer than expected.

contentSections.title: First-trip checklist
items: Working phone number and mobile data or airport Wi-Fi.
Hotel name and street address in Chinese, including the correct airport terminal or railway station.
A primary payment method tested in the app plus a backup card, wallet or cash for an official taxi.
Vehicle plate and driver details matched to the ride record before entering the car.
Use in-app help for a lost item, charge discrepancy or an unresolved unpaid ride.

faqs: Can I pay for DiDi with a foreign credit card?

Some account and ride flows offer supported cards, directly or through a linked wallet. Confirm the payment options shown for your actual booking and complete any issuer verification before you travel.
Does a foreign card in Alipay guarantee DiDi payment?
No. The card, wallet, ride product and transaction must each be accepted. Check the selected method at ride checkout and prepare a backup.
Should I pay the driver in cash if my card is pending?
Check the trip's payment status and your bank first. Do not pay twice for one trip; resolve unclear charges through the ride app's support.
Why is the final DiDi fare higher than the estimate?
Check the trip receipt for traffic, waiting, tolls and product-specific charges, then contact in-app support if a line item looks wrong.
What if payment fails at the airport?
Switch to another method offered in the app or use the airport's official taxi queue. Keep the Chinese address and another usable payment method ready.
